Mission Local’s numbers piece found that San Francisco turnout was 78.9%—slightly above the historical presidential-election average of 77%, but well below 2020’s 86.3%. About 412,000 people voted, roughly 38,000 fewer than in 2020, despite a similar number of registered voters.

It also found sharp geographic divides: Prop. K passed citywide 55–45 even though districts near the Great Highway voted overwhelmingly against it. Daniel Lurie’s mayoral campaign spent $16 million, while Prop. D’s $9.5 million in fundraising did not prevent its defeat. The article also discussed how redistricting affected supervisor races.
